sentences.text: Coloradisaurus is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was estimated to be 3 meters long and weigh 70 kilograms, while the larger species reached 4 meters in length, 2 meters in height, and about 100 kilograms.
Its skull was distinctively high and short, equipped with large eye orbits.
Coloradisaurus is known from two specimens found in the Los Colorados Formation, all discovered in 1971 at the La Esquina locality in Argentina.

The expedition was organized by the Fundación Miguel Lillo with financial support from the National Council of Scientific and Technical Research, involving Martín Vince, Juan C. Leal, Tomás H. Fasola, and José F. Bonaparte.
Modern consensus classifies Coloradisaurus as a massospondylid closely related to Lufengosaurus and Glacialisaurus.

Recent findings suggest Coloradisaurus is the sister taxon of Lufengosaurus and both clearly belong to Massospondylidae, with cladistic analyses finding Coloradisaurus basal to Glacialisaurus within this group.
This animal lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 213 million years ago.
It inhabited South America during the Late Triassic, approximately 218 to 210 million years ago.
It is possible that Coloradisaurus is an adult specimen of Mussaurus.
